chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Abi Nasr, from Dawud ibn Sirhan, from Abdullah ibn Farqad, from Humran, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), when he was prevented at Al-Hudaybiyya, shortened (his hair/nails) and freed from Ihram, and offered a sacrifice. Then he departed from it, and shaving (of the head) was not obligatory upon him until he fulfilled the ritual. So, as for the confined one, only shortening is upon him.
ai.seo_question: What are the ritual obligations for a pilgrim prevented from completing Hajj at Al-Hudaybiyya?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the specific ritual status of the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) during the Treaty of Al-Hudaybiyya, where he was prevented from entering Mecca. It establishes the legal precedent for the 'Mahsur' (one confined or prevented), ruling that shortening the sacrifice (Qasr) is sufficient rather than full shaving (Halq), which becomes obligatory only upon the completion of the Hajj rites. This distinction highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding partial completion of rituals under duress or obstruction.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Abu Nasr, from Dawood Bin Sirham, from Abdullah Bin Farqad, from Humran, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup>

having said that Rasool-Allahsaww, when hesaww was prevented at Al-Hudaybiyya, shortened (hissaww nails, hair etc.), and freed from wearing Ihraam, and offered a sacrifice. Then hesaww left from it. And, the shaving (of the head) is not Obligated until the rituals are fulfilled. So, as for the confined one, rather the shortening (of hair, nails, etc.) happens to be upon him’.
en.sarwar: 1. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ibn abu Nasr from Dawud ibn Sarhan from ‘Abd Allah ibn Farqad from Humran who has said the following: “

When the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause was prevented at al-Hudaybiyah from performing al-Hajj, he (the Messenger of Allah) did Taqsir (cutting some hair or finger nails and so on). He (the Messenger of Allah) then came out of the state of Ihram and offered sacrifice, then left that place. Shaving was not obligatory for him until all acts of al-Hajj are performed. One who is Mahsur (confined) must carry out Taqsir (cutting some hair or finger nails and so on).’”
